overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by not announcing the meeting was being recorded and by failing to declare the detrimental-effect statement before executive session; the other allegations were rejected.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair did not announce at the April 28 meeting that the meeting was being recorded.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Chair did not announce that the meeting was being recorded, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice did not list the names of the candidates to be appointed to a committee subcommittee.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by not including the names of the individuals on the April 28 meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee discussed a 'surround care' summer program that was not listed on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: We credit the Committee’s explanation that the Chair did not reasonably anticipate the need to discuss this topic during the April 28 meeting and find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair failed to make the required declaration that an open meeting may have a detrimental effect on bargaining before entering Purpose 3 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Prior to convening in executive session, Chair Barbosa simply read from the law stating “if an open meeting may have a detrimental effect” on the Committee’s negotiating position but failed to specifically declare that discussions in open session may have a detrimental effect on the Committee’s negotiating position.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee failed to conduct a roll call vote to enter executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Committee voted by roll call to close the open session and then immediately convened in executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a quorum of members deliberated outside a meeting through off-microphone side conversations during the April 28 meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and caution the Committee that a similar, future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
